author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN002667541 (PTHR13390)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel sturkopf (FBgn0035206)

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**
PTN002667541 adds [sterol ester esterase activity](http://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0004771) to members of the [LIPASE (PTHR13390)](http://www.pantherdb.org/panther/family.do?clsAccession=PTHR13390) family, based on a single annotation to:
(MOUSE|MGI=MGI=1916082|UniProtKB=Q8BVA5) from PMID:24357060

However, a different paper (PMID: [23525007](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23525007/)) says that the same mouse protein (MGI:1916082) "lacked detectable neutral lipid lipase activity" and the fly ortholog (sturkopf) "does not act as a neutral lipid hydrolase." The same paper says in its discussion " Although our studies do not rule out that CG9186 exerts a specific or very weak lipolytic activity, its function as a canonical neutral lipid lipase similar to Brummer can be excluded. Despite the fact that CG9186 possesses the diagnostic sequence motif for the catalytic site of lipases, the protein could also act, for example, as an acyltransferase or a phospholipid modifying enzyme, a speculation that will be addressed in future biochemical studies."

The UniProt entry for the mouse protein (Q8BVA5) includes the caution statement "The catalytic activity is unsure despite catalytic sites being conserved"

So...it seems best not to annotate this node with 'sterol ester esterase activity' for the time being?
title: PAINT issue: PTN002667541 (PTHR13390)
